title: Uptime activation tactical runway and sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick living doc for the near-term activation of the Uptime Program: coord plan for rolling SLOs across product areas, what must land in the platform to enable run, and who owns the handoff. This is intentionally tactical — sprint scoped with clear owners and open questions.

Background: 
- Q4 pilot showed good signal alignment but gaps in cross-team alerting and SLI instrumentation.
- Platform needs minor platform-side instrumentation (edge LB metrics + prefix cache hit breakdown) and an oncall runbook template before we scale SLO rollouts.

Objectives (90d):
1) Baseline visibility for all customer-facing routes: p50/p90/p99 latency + error-rate (4xx/5xx) in unified dashboard.
2) Ship per-service SLO definitions and acceptance criteria for 12 high-impact services (targets suggested below).
3) Complete handoff package + runbook for each service (runbook template, alert thresholds, escalation path).
4) Train product on SLO review cadence and incident playbook.

Suggested SLO targets (initial, to be ratified by service owners):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% (monthly) for core inference routes
- p99 latency: < 350ms for interactive endpoints (hosted tier)
- Error-rate SLO: 0.2% (5xx)

Scope:
- In scope: hosted API routes, dedicated ingress lanes, internal model-serving control-plane surfaces.
- Out of scope: third-party integrations, long-tail batch jobs (phase 2).

Stakeholders & RACI: 
- Platform eng (owner): Maya Chen — platform instrumentation, dashboard templates, rollout cadence
- SRE (accountable): Liam O'Connor — alert config, runbook acceptance, oncall playbook updates
- Product: Asha Patel — define service-level impact & customer risk, accept SLOs for product features
- Observability: Diego Morales — metric naming standard, cost/retention plan
- Solutions Eng / CS: Rina Sato — customer impact validation for high-value customers

90-day tactical runway (high level):
- Week 0–2: finalize SLO template + shared dashboard skeleton. Deliverables: SLO template PR, dashboard wireframe. (Owner: Maya / Diego)
- Week 3–5: Instrument top-12 services (traces + SLIs). Deliverables: metric collections validated, test alerts. (Owner: Platform & service owners)
- Week 6–8: Canary SLOs in non-prod; runbook writeups; tabletop drills for two services. Deliverables: drill notes, runbook drafts. (Owner: SRE)
- Week 9–12: Prod rollout for first tranche of services; oncall rotation updates; post-launch evaluation. Deliverables: postmortem template, acceptance signoffs. (Owner: Product + SRE)

Sprint-level tasks (examples / not exhaustive):
- Platform: add edge LB -> service latency histogram + tag by route, prefix-cache hit rate metric, sampling rate for traces (TODO: confirm tracer cost).
- SRE: create templated alert rules (pageable + paging exempt) and a runbook checklist (severity mapping, mitigation steps, fallback route).
- Observability: standardize metric names, add dashboard panels, configure retention/aggregation windows.
- Product owners: review suggested SLOs, document acceptable maintenance windows, and customer-facing degradation messaging.

Risk register (top items):
1) Missing signal due to nonstandard metric names — mitigation: obs team to run a metric inventory first 2 weeks.
2) Pager fatigue from noisy alerts — mitigation: default to 3-tier alerting and use paging-exempt escalation for gradual degradation.
3) Cost of high-resolution metrics/traces — mitigation: sampling + tiered retention; validate with Diego.
4) Non-consensus from product on SLO targets — mitigation: escalate to GTM/PD for business-level tradeoffs; schedule SLA vs SLO workshop.

Monitoring & dashboards: 
- Required panels: SLI trend (7d/30d), incident count by service, error budget burn (rolling 7d & monthly), top 10 latency outliers by route.
- Alerting thresholds: burn rate > 4x for 30m for paging; soft alerts for feature teams at 2x.

Handoff checklist (per service):
- SLO definition doc linked in service repo
- Dashboard + query examples in observability
- Runbook completed and loaded into oncall tool
- Escalation path and contact list validated
- Post-launch acceptance signoff by product & SRE

Communications plan: 
- Weekly sync (30m) with engineering leads during instrument phase (Weeks 1–6).
- Biweekly stakeholder demo + signoff session once canary begins.
- Slack channel: #uptime-activation (setup by Platform) and a pinned meeting notes doc.

Acceptance criteria for rollout: 
- Instrumentation shows <5% missing samples for required SLIs during test window.
- Runbook passes a tabletop drill (2 of 3 critical steps executed within target times).
- Product owner signoff recorded in linked artifact (confluence doc or GH issue).

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Q1: Should model-serving control-plane metrics be included in the same SLO, or separate control-plane SLOs? (Decision: Product + SRE)
- Q2: Reserved capacity vs. burst capacity impact on SLO attribution (how to credit infra-level throttles). Need doc from infra team.
- Q3: Sampling rate for traces to keep cost under $X/month — Diego to propose.

Next steps (owners and TLDR):
- Maya: finalize SLO template and submit PR by 2026-02-17.
- Diego: run metric inventory and share gaps by 2026-02-20.
- Liam: draft runbook template and alert rules by 2026-02-24.
- Asha: schedule product review workshop 2026-02-25.

Notes / scratch: 
- TODO: map services to owners (need updated service registry export)
- TODO: confirm retention budget with finance for increased metric retention
- Quick wins: toggle to aggregate p99 across regions first, then narrow by route

Meeting minutes snapshot (2026-02-11 quick sync):
- Agreed to prefer availability SLO over per-endpoint SLA in initial rollout to reduce scope.
- Observability to own metric renaming spike (2 days), platform to add dash panels following that.
- Action: product to mark top 12 services and confirm business impact by EOD 2026-02-12.

File notes: living doc — move to final "activation runbook" in Confluence once program completes Phase 1.
